name: overnight-20

messages.subject: The Friday Byte: 10 things worth reading this week
body_lines: The Friday Byte, issue 212
1. Why small models are getting better at structured output. Researchers compared quantized models on extraction tasks and found that constrained decoding closes much of the gap with larger models.
2. A field guide to calendar time zones. Daylight saving time ends this weekend in much of North America, and the usual bugs are back: meetings an hour off and recurring events that drift.
3. The quiet return of desktop apps. More teams are shipping local-first software that works offline and syncs later, and users seem to like owning their data.
4. How to write a good bug report. Steps to reproduce, what you expected, what happened, and the version you ran. Screenshots help, but logs help more.
5. Keyboard shortcuts you should know. A short list for every major operating system, from window snapping to quick search.
6. Interview: running a two-person software company. Two founders talk about pricing, support and saying no to features.
7. Battery life on modern laptops. Integrated graphics have improved enough that light inference workloads no longer drain a battery in an hour.
8. A reading list on privacy engineering. Data minimization, purpose limitation and why logs are the most common leak.
9. Tool of the week: a tiny command-line timer that keeps you honest about breaks.
10. From the archive: our 2024 piece on writing release notes people actually read.
You are receiving this because you subscribed at fridaybyte.example.com. Unsubscribe or change your preferences at any time.
